design_rationale:
WORKLOG / DOSSIER - task 1 (service_contract_claims_and_cancellations).
[Step 0 draw] draw_counts.py --task 1 printed {"prerequisite_problems": 3, "problems": 4, "factor_counts": [4, 6, 6, 5]}; the tree is the root plus three prerequisite problems; factor counts: overpayment recovery 4, trip interruption 6, repair payment 6, diagnostic payment 5 (multiset [4, 5, 6, 6] = the draw).
[Scope snapshot] Occupied by task 0: warranty_ext_cancellation_settlement, warranty_ext_stack_remainder_authorization, warranty_ext_rental_reimbursement_settlement and tools cancel_plan_with_refund_1804bd93, authorize_stack_remainder_2296c771, file_rental_reimbursement_5fdd83af. Claimed here (disjoint): warranty_ext_trip_interruption_reimbursement (root, file_trip_interruption_claim_d37559b2, user), warranty_ext_release_repair_payment (pay_repair_facility_1c2b8918), warranty_ext_diagnostic_time_payment (pay_diagnostic_time_6cc9f33c), warranty_ext_claim_overpayment_recovery (recover_overpaid_claim_bcfb33cc). After this task every extended policy of the difficulty is claimed; nothing is reserved.
[Why a good test] The caller asks only for her hotel and meals. The trip rule says the reimbursement is not fixed until the facility has been paid for the repair work on the stranding repair order; the repair-payment rule says it waits on a recovery of every overpaid claim payment and on the diagnostic payment; the diagnostic rule says it is not booked until the overpaid payment carries its recovery. The agent must read those sentences, find in the ledger that payment 7fb78265-79e7-44f8-9dce-36852f391975 (1480.00) exceeds its decision 4687ba00-3fa8-46ac-a530-4af0f9d3c8e9 (1180.00) with no recovery and that RO-558204 has no payment at all, work out recovery -> diagnostic -> repair payment, and compute four amounts whose inputs chain through the coverage remaining (5120.00 -> 5401.5 -> 4889.62) and through the repair-order payments (4658.57) into the trip figure.
[Problem-tree card] root warranty_ext_trip_interruption_reimbursement. Edge warranty_ext_trip_interruption_reimbursement -> warranty_ext_release_repair_payment: value_input on ro_paid_total, ACTION form (fallback: the repair payment and the diagnostic payment are the same kind of entry on the same repair order, so no record state singles out the repair-work payment), sentence: "A trip interruption reimbursement is not fixed until the facility has been paid for the repair work on the repair order that stranded the holder."; false at opening: no payment on RO-558204. Resolved by pay_repair_facility_1c2b8918 (agent). Edge warranty_ext_release_repair_payment -> warranty_ext_claim_overpayment_recovery: value_input on coverage_now, state form: "The payment of an approved decision is worked out only after every claim payment on the plan that exceeds the approved amount of the decision it settled carries a recovery entry."; false: 7fb78265-79e7-44f8-9dce-36852f391975 1480.00 > 4687ba00-3fa8-46ac-a530-4af0f9d3c8e9 1180.00, no recovery names it; the only write of a recovery entry is recover_overpaid_claim_bcfb33cc. Edge warranty_ext_release_repair_payment -> warranty_ext_diagnostic_time_payment: value_input on coverage_now, ACTION form (same fallback reason): "The repair payment on a decision is figured only after the facility's diagnostic time on that repair order has been paid."; resolved by pay_diagnostic_time_6cc9f33c. Edge warranty_ext_diagnostic_time_payment -> warranty_ext_claim_overpayment_recovery: state_gate, state form, negated direction: "A diagnostic time payment is not booked until every claim payment on the plan that exceeds the approved amount of the decision it settled carries a recovery entry.". Four-point test: each carries an ordering connective (not ... until / only after / only after / not ... until); state forms name entries on the ledger, action forms name the business action; no tool, id or code token; 'every' matches the condition's scope. Directions follow the business voice (a reimbursement or a booking 'is not ... until', a figure 'is worked out only after'). Topological order warranty_ext_claim_overpayment_recovery -> warranty_ext_diagnostic_time_payment -> warranty_ext_release_repair_payment -> warranty_ext_trip_interruption_reimbursement, unique. Deletion sensitivity: skip recovery -> repair payment 3907.97; skip diagnostic -> repair payment 4580.8; skip repair payment -> trip 365.62; gold 4146.69 / 597.66.
[Base-invariant card] Recovery (warranty_claim_payment_recovered): warranty_claims has no structured gate on this subject (policy_scope); the 180-day recovery window from 2026-07-24 runs to 2027-01-20 - 74 days used. Diagnostic and repair payments (warranty_claim_paid): warranty_claims.pay_on_active - contract 6ec39aa6-5508-4749-8ae6-eed4bae2de47 active (evidence status); Platinum diagnostic_covered_when_repair_covered true. Trip (warranty_benefit_reimbursed): warranty_benefits.benefit_state - active; approved claim on RO-558204 (85841b07-9e7a-43dd-846b-a2a41368db00); breakdown about 500 miles from the Austin address (minimum 100); trip receipts within Platinum's 30 benefit receipt submission days counted from the release date (the latest claim payment on RO-558204, 2026-10-06 - day 0) and one trip benefit per repair order - none yet on RO-558204; both are stated in the trip rule and carried in its compute (trip_receipt_window_open, trip_already_paid). No time-kind eligibility applies (temporal_feasibility []).
[Business-object card] Contract 6ec39aa6-5508-4749-8ae6-eed4bae2de47 (Platinum, VIN 5FNRL6H73KB509318). Recovery object: payment 7fb78265-79e7-44f8-9dce-36852f391975 -> decision 4687ba00-3fa8-46ac-a530-4af0f9d3c8e9 (RO-556204) by source_txn_id; the steering overpayment e45e9b18-6170-48d3-8cfc-7154029004ac is excluded because recovery 73d309bc-52cc-4f98-8c91-3e036c3ca67b already names it. Payment object: decision 85841b07-9e7a-43dd-846b-a2a41368db00 (RO-558204) - the most recent approved decision; both new payments carry it as source and RO-558204 as repair order. Trip object: RO-558204; the March trip reimbursement 5f84d6d6-2b73-426e-b36a-a5098ab59827 on RO-553078 is a different repair order and only feeds the recent-trip share.
[Factor card - recovery, 4] payment_error_measure (method, multi-source: decision result + payment amount on every tier): 300.00 (baseline whole payment -> 1290.4); aged_recovery_share 0.9 (74 days; baseline -> 310.0); facility_collection_share 0.95 (independent; -> 295.0); repeat_error_handling 25.00 (one recovery in twelve months; -> 256.5). Fall-back 1480.0.
[Factor card - diagnostic, 5] diagnostic_system_hours 2.0 (engine; -> 365.62); program_equipment_hours +0.5 (Kestrel Certified, cross purchase; -> 438.75); long_diagnosis_adjustment +1.0 h (4 days; method; -> 365.62); repeat_diagnosis_share 0.75 (engine decided 2026-03-16; -> 682.5); diagnostic_hourly_rate 195.00 (franchise; -> 459.38). Fall-back 175.0.
[Factor card - repair payment, 6] limited_decision_refigure (method): approved 5120.00 above coverage now 4889.62 -> 4889.62 (-> 4342.07); facility_agreement_allowance 0.02 (-> 4231.32); exchanged_unit_core_credit 0.04 (-> 4319.47); comeback_repair_share 0.85 (-> 4878.46); parts_program_uplift 0.05 (cross purchase; -> 3949.23); late_payment_interest 0.01 (3 days; -> 4105.64). Fall-back 4889.62.
[Factor card - trip, 6] failure_day_count (parameter): +1 because the decision came 4 days after the 2026-09-29 failure (-> 557.81); trip_day_cap 7 (payments 4658.57 on the engine, multi-source; -> 517.97); overflow_day_payment (method): 8 trip days exceed the cap of 7 on an engine repair, so the day beyond the cap is paid at the 0.5 overflow-day share - 7.5 allowance-days (baseline: capped days only -> 557.81; the other tier would pay the day beyond at the 35.00 meals amount); program_trip_allowance 125.00 (cross purchase; -> 478.12); recent_trip_share 0.75 (March trip; -> 796.88); repair_coverage_share 0.85 (-> 703.12). Fall-back 500.0 (7 days from failure to release, capped at 5, at 100.00). Near-misses: the March trip falls just outside six months (2026-03-20 to 2026-10-06 = 6 whole months, not within the last six), the steering overpayment is already recovered, and the earlier engine decision is outside three months.
[Seed rows and why] customer; Kestrel Certified purchase order (program for three factors); Platinum contract with coverage remaining 5120.00 equal to the ledger; ledger of 14 rows: limit; five decisions and their payments (transmission, A/C, steering overpaid and recovered, engine, brakes overpaid) giving the coverage history, the comeback/repeat evidence and the recovery target; the January recovery (handling charge); the March trip reimbursement (recent-trip share); the approved RO-558204 decision limited to 5120.00 (the object of both payments and the trip). No unsettled status outside the tree.
[Persona] Nadia, a band director stranded in Amarillo; volunteers the breakdown, tow, the dealership's Saturday approval and that the van is ready, and asks for hotel and meals; identity, distance, RO number, receipts and the March trip only when asked; files once with the values given; closes when told the filing went through and the amount.
[Standard solution] Locate, verify, read contract, ledger and purchase order; recover 281.5 on 7fb78265-79e7-44f8-9dce-36852f391975; pay diagnostic time 511.88; pay the repair work 4146.69; hand over the trip filing: 8 days, 597.66.
[Verification] _authoring.evaluate replays the gold writes and evaluates each compute at steps 6, 8, 10, 12: 281.5, 511.88, 4146.69, 597.66; factor baselines, fall-backs and skip runs as listed; check_compute recomputes the same.
[Closure] warranty_ext_claim_overpayment_recovery -> recover_overpaid_claim_bcfb33cc -> 6/recovery_amount; warranty_ext_diagnostic_time_payment -> pay_diagnostic_time_6cc9f33c -> 8/payment_amount; warranty_ext_release_repair_payment -> pay_repair_facility_1c2b8918 -> 10/payment_amount; warranty_ext_trip_interruption_reimbursement -> file_trip_interruption_claim_d37559b2 -> 12/reimbursement_amount. Terminal: recovery, two payments, trip reimbursement, coverage remaining 742.93.
[Draft recomputation from visible context] From the published rules, tool schemas, the three finder returns and the caller's lines the same four writes and values follow; the only caller-supplied argument is RO-558204, which the ledger also shows.
[Revision log] v1 - initial design. v2 (policy-task audit round 1): F-D-1 / F-1-1 - the trip computation's two method labels only selected an operand of one day-count expression -> the end-day ladder is retired as a factor (the release date is now plain rule text: the latest claim payment on the repair order, or the decision date where none has posted, which is also the baseline), the failure-day count is relabelled parameter, and a genuine method factor is added: overflow_day_payment, whose tiers pay the days beyond the cap at a share of the allowance (engine or transmission), at a flat meals amount with no lodging (other repairs), or not at all (baseline). To make it bite the RO-558204 failure date moved from 2026-09-30 to 2026-09-29 (persona updated: the breakdown and the first hotel night are September 29), so 8 trip days exceed the cap of 7. Diagnostic days became 4 (same tier, 511.88 unchanged); release payment unchanged 4146.69; trip now 8 days, 597.66 (sensitivities 557.81 / 517.97 / 557.81 / 478.12 / 796.88 / 703.12, fall-back 500.0; skipping the repair payment gives 365.62). O-7 - the trip rule now restates that it applies only when the breakdown happened at least the plan's trip interruption minimum distance from the holder's residential address (the caller states about five hundred miles). Tool docstrings now say 'rounded to the nearest cent' instead of 'half up'. All per-task gates re-run green. v3 (policy-task audit round 2, task PASS - no scored value changed): rounding observation - the round-2 note above claimed the half-cent ties were dealt with; they were not, and the record now says exactly what happens: the non-scored figures 365.62 (diagnostic system-hours and long-diagnosis baselines, and the skip-release run), 478.12 and 703.12 are exact half-cent values (365.625, 478.125, 703.125) that the gate's evaluator rounds with Python round() on binary floats, which sends each of them to the lower cent; the gate requires the declared figure to equal that evaluator, so they are recorded as 365.62 / 478.12 / 703.12. No scored argument of this task sits on a half-cent tie (281.50, 511.875 -> 511.88 in either convention, 4146.694, 597.65625 -> 597.66 in either convention), so the tool contract's 'nearest cent' fixes every scored value uniquely. O-11 - the trip rule now states its own receipt window (from the release date, a recorded payment date) and the once-per-repair-order limit, and the compute carries both; values unchanged (window day 0, no trip entry on RO-558204). Full number sweep of every prose field re-checked against the world and the recomputation: no other figure needed correction. v4 (policy-task audit round 3, task PASS): O-1-2 - the March trip row was priced at the base 100.00 allowance; it is now priced by the trip rule in force on its own date, evaluated with the gate's evaluator on the 2026-03-20 world: 6 trip days x 125.00 = 750.00 (benefit_days 6); the row is still read only by the recent-trip share, which counts its existence, so no scored value moves. After the round-3 charter change (rental only) every skip and sensitivity figure of this task was re-evaluated rather than carried forward: recovery 281.5 (1290.4 / 310.0 / 295.0 / 256.5, all-baseline 1480.0); diagnostic 511.88 (365.62 / 438.75 / 365.62 / 682.5 / 459.38, all-baseline 175.0), without step 6 = 511.88; repair payment 4146.69 (4342.07 / 4231.32 / 4319.47 / 4878.46 / 3949.23 / 4105.64, all-baseline 4889.62), without step 6 = 3907.97, without step 8 = 4580.8; trip 597.66 (557.81 / 517.97 / 557.81 / 478.12 / 796.88 / 703.12, all-baseline 500.0), without step 10 = 365.62 - all equal to the figures stated above.
user_scenario: You are Nadia Valdivia, a 47-year-old high-school band director from Austin, Texas: warm, organized, a little frazzled after a week away from home with two teenagers. You bought a 2019 Honda Odyssey EX-L from Kestrel Auto in April 2024 with a KestrelCare plan. On September 29 the van's engine failed on I-40 near Amarillo, about five hundred miles from home, and it was towed to Panhandle Honda, the Honda dealership in Amarillo. The dealership told you on Saturday, October 3, that KestrelCare had approved the engine repair, and this morning they told you the van is finished and you can pick it up today. You open with roughly: "Hi, my van broke down on the way to Colorado and I've been stuck in a hotel in Amarillo for almost a week. My KestrelCare plan covers trip interruption, right? I'd like my hotel and meals reimbursed." You want the trip interruption reimbursement for your hotel and meals settled on this call, and you are happy for the representative to take care of whatever Kestrel has to book on its side today. You give your identity details only when asked, one or two at a time: your mobile number is 5125555607, your date of birth is 1979-02-17, and the last four of your Social Security number are 5391. You do not know any contract reference numbers. If asked how far from home the breakdown happened, you say about five hundred miles, in Amarillo, and that you live in Austin. If asked for the repair order number, you read it off the dealership's paperwork: RO-558204. If asked about receipts, you say you kept every hotel and restaurant receipt since the night of September 29. If asked whether KestrelCare has paid for a trip like this before, you say yes, once in March when the van broke down near Dallas. If the representative explains that you have to file the trip interruption claim yourself and hands you the step to do it, you complete it once with exactly the repair order number, the number of days and the amount the representative gives you, and then tell the representative it went through. You do not question the amount the representative states; you simply ask them to go ahead. Once the representative confirms your trip interruption reimbursement has been filed and states the amount, you thank them and end the call; you do not raise anything else.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: Every pair is ordered by a prerequisite sentence: the diagnostic payment waits on the recovery ('A diagnostic time payment is not booked until ...'), the repair payment waits on both the recovery and the diagnostic payment, and the trip reimbursement waits on the repair payment, so recovery -> diagnostic -> repair payment -> trip filing is the only topological order. The recovery must precede the diagnostic payment also because the recovery reads the plan's most recent claim payment; booked after the diagnostic payment it would read the wrong payment - the sentence pins this order rather than leaving it to the reader.

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Skipping step 10: reimbursement_amount recomputes to 365.62 (exactly 365.625, which the gate's evaluator rounds down) instead of 597.66 (only the 511.88 diagnostic payment on RO-558204: the release date is still 2026-10-06, but the payments stay below 1000.00 so the cap is 5, the three days beyond it are paid at the 0.5 overflow share - 6.5 allowance-days - and the coverage share falls to 0.6), and the terminal ledger lacks the repair payment.
Skipping step 6: payment_amount at step 10 recomputes to 3907.97 instead of 4146.69 (coverage remaining 4608.12 without the recovery), and the terminal ledger lacks the recovery.
Skipping step 8: payment_amount at step 10 recomputes to 4580.8 instead of 4146.69 (coverage remaining 5401.5), and the terminal ledger lacks the diagnostic payment.
Skipping step 6 leaves the diagnostic amount at 511.88 but the terminal ledger lacks the recovery and the coverage remaining ends 281.5 lower; the state gate is what releases payments on the plan.
